B.</ls>; <ls>T. 4. 28</ls> नाभ्यासकममीक्षते <ls>Pt. 1. 151</ls>; <ls>Ms. 12. 74</ls>; <ls>Y. 3. 322</ls>. <ab>cf.</ab> also अन्यायश्च कृतेऽभ्यासः . <ls>MS. 10. 3. 26</ls> .²2 Repeated practice or exercise, continued practice or use; अविरतश्रमाभ्यासात् <ls>K. 30</ls>; <ls>Pt. 1. 133</ls>; अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते <ls>Bg. 6. 35</ls>, <ls n="Bg. 6.">44</ls> by constant practice (to remain pure and unmodified); <ls n="Bg.">12. 12</ls>; योग˚ <ls>Y. 3. 51</ls> practice of concentration; hence sometimes used for ‘concentration of mind upon one subject’; ˚निगृहीतेन मनसा <ls>R. 10. 23</ls>; so शर˚, अस्त्र˚ <ab>&c.</ab> .²3 Habit, custom, practice; मिथ्योपपदात् कृञोऽभ्यासे <ls>P. I. 3. 71</ls>; तद् यथाभ्यासम् अभिधीयताम् <ls>U. 1</ls> therefore address me as is your wont; अमङ्गलाभ्यासरतिम् <ls>Ku. 5. 65</ls>; <ls>Y. 3. 68</ls>. .²4 Discipline in arms, exercise, military discipline. .²5 Reciting, study, repeated reading or learning by heart; काव्यज्ञशिक्षयाभ्यासः <ls>K. P. 1</ls>; <ls>K. 146</ls>, <ls n="K.">200</ls>; <ls>Ms. 5. 4</ls>; वेद˚ is of 5 kinds:-- वेदस्वीकरणं पूर्वं विचारोऽभ्यसनं जपः . तद्दानं चैव शिष्येभ्यो वेदाभ्यासो हि पञ्चधा .. <ls>Dakṣa.</ls> .²6 vicinity, proximity, neighbourhood (for अभ्याश); चूतयष्टिरिवाभ्यासे (शे) मधौ परभृतोन्मुखी <ls>Ku. 6. 2</ls>; (अभ्यासे-शे मधौ must mean here speaking to ‘Madhu who was {%near%} her’ {%<ab>scil.</ab>%} by having manifested himself before her, which fully preserves the simile of Pārvatī, herself silent, speaking to her lover who was near her through her friend); अर्पितेयं तवाभ्यासे सीता पुण्यव्रता वधूः <ls>U. 7. 17</ls> given in your charge; <ls>Śi. 3. 40</ls>; अभ्यासा(शा)दागतः <ls>P. II. 1. 38. Sk.</ls> (regarded as an Aluk Compound). .²7 (In <ab>gram.</ab>) Reduplication. .²8 The first syllable of a reduplicated base, reduplicative syllable; पूर्वोऽभ्यासः <ls>P. VI. 1. 4</ls>; अत्र ये द्वे विहिते तयोः पूर्वोऽभ्याससंज्ञः स्यात् <ls>Sk.</ls> .²9 (In <ab>Math.</ab>) Multiplication. .²10 (In poetry) Repetition of the last verses or lines (as of a chorus); chorus, burden of a song.
